# Why Hē is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Hē** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Hē has no myth in the traditional sense. Its 'mythology' is the history of interpretation: how a tiny grammatical word became, for some philosophers, a divine name. Plato calls the principle of matter the hupodochē, the 'receptacle' of all becoming.  It receives forms the way a mother receives seed.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Hē
- **ASCII form:** he
- **Meaning:** "Feminine nominative singular article in Ancient Greek; in Orphic and Neoplatonic thought, the receptacle of divine overflow and counterpart to τὸ ἕν (Hén)."
- **Domain of influence:** The Divine Feminine Principle, She Who Is
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** ἡ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 94 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **ἡ**. On the evidence, it means "Feminine nominative singular article in Ancient Greek; in Orphic and Neoplatonic thought, the receptacle of divine overflow and counterpart to τὸ ἕν (Hén).".

Strip **Hē** to *he* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **e → ē** — Macron marks long e: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

None of these marks is decoration. Each one is a fact about how the name was spoken, and each one is checkable against the scholarly record the temple cites.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Hē** lives at [/sites/he/](/sites/he/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/he/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/he/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/he/patterns/).

The restoration preserves one decisive feature the ASCII form drops — a single, honest mark — which places it in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Hē** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Women's Health & Femtech** — She Who Is; the divine feminine principle itself.
- **Astrology, Tarot & Esoteric Services** — Neoplatonic theurgy named her; grammatical mysticism is the esoteric tradition's own method.
- **Philosophy, Ethics & Standards** — She Who Is; the feminine principle of Neoplatonic thought.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
